model_annotation: This line plot compares the performance of four Llama model variants—Llama-3B, Llama-3B + FT, Llama-1B, and Llama-1B + FT—across a range of input sizes or steps labeled from 'r0' to 'r8' on the x-axis, which appears to represent a discrete progression (possibly related to rank, resolution, or iteration) with no explicit units. The y-axis, ranging from approximately 2 to 9 with major gridlines at intervals of 2, likely represents a performance metric such as accuracy, score, or efficiency, though no unit is specified. The blue solid line with circular markers for Llama-3B starts at ~4.2 at r0 and rises steadily to ~8.4 at r8. The green dashed line with triangular markers for Llama-3B + FT begins at ~5.0 at r0 and increases to ~8.5 at r8, showing a slightly higher performance than Llama-3B across most points. The light blue solid line with circular markers for Llama-1B starts at ~2.8 at r0 and climbs to ~8.2 at r8, beginning lower but converging near the top. The light green dashed line with triangular markers for Llama-1B + FT starts at ~3.5 at r0 and reaches ~8.3 at r8, also showing consistent improvement and tracking closely with Llama-1B. All models exhibit a generally increasing trend, with fine-tuned versions (indicated by “+ FT”) performing better than their base counterparts at nearly all points.
